steps.body: A number line shows the multiplication as a journey: each group is one jump, and every jump is the same length.
steps.narration: A number line shows the multiplication as a journey: each group is one jump, and every jump is the same length.

widget.prompt: On a FIFTHS line, place where 2 × 2/5 lands.

commonPlacements.feedback: 2/5 is one jump. Two were asked for.

widget.successFeedback: 4/5 — two jumps of two fifths each, landing one fifth short of the whole.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — each jump covers two fifths, so two jumps reach four of them.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — 5/5 is the whole, and two jumps of two fifths stop one fifth short of it.

predict.prompt: Three jumps of 2/5 from zero land where?
predict.reveal: Each jump covers two fifths, so three jumps cover six — one more than the five fifths in a whole.

cml.actionGoal: Collect equal groups of a fraction and watch only the COUNT of pieces change for g4x line model.
invariants: Multiplying a fraction by a whole number collects groups of identical pieces: the denominator names the piece size and holds still, while the numerator counts every piece gathered, which is what keeps g4x line model a counting problem.
misconceptions: Scaling the denominator along with the numerator, adding the whole number to the numerator, or assuming a product cannot pass one whole.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the denominator DID change when you collected groups, what would happen to the size of each piece?

widget.prompt: On a number line marked in fifths, how do you show 3 × 2/5?

options.label: Three jumps of 2/5 each, landing on 6/5
options.feedback: Correct — each jump is two fifths long, and three of them cover six fifths, just past one whole.

options.label: One jump of 3/5
options.feedback: That is a single group of three fifths; the expression asks for three groups of two fifths.

options.label: Two jumps of 3/5, landing on 6/5
options.feedback: It lands correctly by accident, but it models 2 × 3/5 — a different story with a different group size.

options.label: Three jumps of 1/5
options.feedback: That is 3 × 1/5 = 3/5; each jump here must be two fifths, not one.

widget.prompt: Compute 4 × 2/4 as ?/4. What is the numerator?

commonErrors.feedback: That multiplied the whole number by the DENOMINATOR; the piece size stays put and only the count scales.
That is one group's numerator — 4 groups of 2 fourths were asked for.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Count the same-size pieces the groups collect; the denominator never changes.
